description:
Keep Wifi-ADB active and toggle it from a tile or widget
KeepADB helps keep Wifi-ADB, Android’s “Wireless debugging”, available across device restarts, Wi-Fi reconnects, access-point changes, and idle periods.

Toggle Wifi-ADB from the main screen, a Quick Settings tile, or a home-screen widget. An optional foreground service monitors the connection and attempts recovery when Android disables it. Android may ask for approval to enable Wifi-ADB on Wi-Fi. Approve only expected prompts on a private network you trust. Select “Always allow on this network” if you want Android to allow Wifi-ADB automatically when your device reconnects to that network. KeepADB cannot grant this Android approval itself; its trusted-network rule is separate and only controls where automatic recovery may run. If Android does not confirm an automatic enable, KeepADB backs off instead of retrying rapidly.

Features:
* Quick Settings tile, main app controls, and launcher shortcuts (Toggle Wifi-ADB, Wi-Fi networks, Settings)
* Tap the endpoint to copy the adb connect command; “Connect a computer…” below it, and the last page of the setup assistant, explain how to pair a new computer
* Two home-screen widgets: KeepADB controls grows with its size (Wifi-ADB, Keep-Alive, webhook auto-sync; main action and order per widget), KeepADB overview shows the endpoint, Wi-Fi, Keep-Alive and webhook delivery at a glance
* Optional Keep-Alive service across restarts and network changes
* Endpoint discovery through Android NSD/mDNS (_adb-tls-connect._tcp); timing depends on network conditions
* Optional HTTP(S) webhook, disabled by default, for verified Wifi-ADB endpoints, with opt-in periodic refresh (15 min to 23 h 59 min); the main screen shows its status or a shortcut to set it up
* Configurable status notification and endpoint display
* Four optional privacy switches that hide names and addresses in the app, in notifications, and in widgets and the tile, and keep notifications off the lock screen
* Protection page: choose where Keep-Alive may re-enable Wifi-ADB, with a Wi-Fi networks list to trust, block, and name access points; optional Force mode, for a chosen time or until you end it
* 19 interface languages and right-to-left layout support
* No advertising, analytics, tracking, or third-party runtime libraries

On fresh installs, Keep-Alive re-enables Wifi-ADB automatically only at access points you have trusted; existing installations keep their previous network setting. Recognizing trusted networks requires precise Android location access. KeepADB's Keep-Alive service is set up so that identity stays readable in the background too, as long as it was started while the app was open; recovery can still pause if the permission is missing or approximate, or location is off. A service instance that has only ever been started in the background (e.g. after a restart or an app update) keeps the identity masked until the app is opened again, unless you also grant Location "Allow all the time" on KeepADB's Android permission page — an optional step offered in the setup assistant and as a warning on the main screen while trusted networks are required. KeepADB cannot grant this for you and, as with all location access here, only uses it to identify the Wi-Fi network; it does not read or store your location.

KeepADB does not require root. Android protects the Wifi-ADB setting with the WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS permission, so initial setup requires granting it once — directly on the phone via self-pairing in the setup assistant (Android 11+, no computer needed), in a computer browser at https://keepadb.roteson.de/setup (Chrome/Edge over WebUSB), or manually over USB with ADB:

adb shell pm grant de.hohnepeople.keepadb android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

Wifi-ADB exposes an authenticated development service on the connected network. Use Keep-Alive on networks you trust, turn Wifi-ADB off on public hotspots, and reject unexpected Android approval or pairing prompts.
